tasks.short: Review forensic reports for technical merit

steps.what: Review forensic reports against source evidence, method limitations and the strength of stated conclusions

tasks.design: Keep technical merit review with the technician using source evidence in {DOCS}. Native document comparisons can assist navigation, while judging the validity and strength of forensic conclusions remains independent human review.
tasks.previous_blocker: Technical merit depends on evidence quality, method applicability and qualified interpretation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing controlled evidence records support review without replacing its judgement.
tasks.still_hard: A polished report can conceal unsupported inference or omitted contrary evidence.
tasks.human_edge: The reviewer challenges conclusions rather than merely checking document completeness.
tasks.altitude: No assumed change in review effort or acceptance authority.

reach.learn: Explain precisely which inference exceeds the evidence and what correction is needed.

evidence.claim: Independent technical merit review remains human judgement, based on model knowledge; no applicable digest capability replaces it.

assumptions: Boundary is technical review and correction requests, excluding original analysis and formal external release.
Reviewer evaluates raw evidence and method limitations in s1; no free structured correctness or admissibility flag is assumed.
Consider native document navigation first. Zero upkeep because no new model or workflow is introduced.
research_questions: Can an independent reviewer identify omitted contrary findings and overstated conclusions?

already_counted.description: All independent technical review and correction requests remain counted.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gross=0 net=0. Technical merit review remains intact without assuming document completeness equals correctness.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Interpret laboratory findings and test results to classify evidence with explicit uncertainty

tasks.design: Retain evidence interpretation with the technician using findings and references in {DOCS}. Existing analytical summaries support comparison, while the meaning of a result and its limitations remain professional judgement.
tasks.previous_blocker: Mixed materials, contamination and method limits complicate classification.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing references and controlled findings support assessment without replacing it.
tasks.still_hard: An instrument match may not establish a unique material or the relevance of its presence.
tasks.human_edge: The technician distinguishes analytical compatibility from an unsupported categorical conclusion.
tasks.altitude: No assumed reduction in forensic interpretation effort.

reach.task: Integrate laboratory findings into case hypotheses
reach.learn: Communicate classification limits and alternative explanations.

evidence.claim: Forensic classification requires contextual interpretation, based on model knowledge; the digest supplies no applicable validated classifier.

assumptions: Boundary is general interpretation, excluding specialised toxicology, toolmark comparison and independent report review covered by other tasks.

Laboratory personnel produce findings and control records through separately scoped testing before this task. Technician checks applicability here; no automatic result-validity or classification flag is assumed.
Native reference tools are considered first. Zero upkeep because no new automation is proposed.
research_questions: Which apparent classifications require independent confirmatory evidence?

already_counted.description: All contextual interpretation and uncertainty assessment remain counted.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gross=0 net=0. Contextual evidence classification remains fully human and specialised tasks are not counted twice.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Compare objects and impression marks while evaluating correspondence, differences and examination limitations

tasks.design: Keep impression comparison with the technician using the comparison microscope workstation {OTHER}. Existing measurement aids support observation, while evaluating correspondence and attribution limits remains expert examination.
tasks.previous_blocker: Partial marks, wear and material deformation complicate correspondence.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing comparison tools assist inspection without establishing unique source attribution.
tasks.still_hard: Similar observed features can have more than one explanation.
tasks.human_edge: The technician recognises exclusionary differences and states when attribution is inconclusive.
tasks.altitude: No assumed change in comparison effort or conclusion rights.

reach.learn: Preserve the distinction between observed correspondence and strength of attribution.

evidence.claim: Retaining object-to-mark examination is model knowledge; no applicable automated attribution capability appears in the digest.

assumptions: Boundary is comparison of recovered objects and marks; scene collection and formal testimony are separate.
OTHER means comparison microscope workstation. Technician produces observations and limitations during s1; no precomputed match or uniqueness flag is assumed.
Consider native comparison aids first. Zero upkeep because no new capture or automated workflow is introduced.
research_questions: Which observed differences exclude the candidate object and which remain explained by deformation?

already_counted.description: All examination and qualified attribution judgement remain counted.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gross=0 net=0. Physical comparison and interpretation remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Identify and quantify drugs or poisons

steps.what: Identify drugs or poisons through specimen analysis and checked calibration and control observations
Calculate concentrations from checked calibration, specimen quantities and dilution factors
Check quantification and identification against source observations before accepting the analytical result

tasks.design: Use native validated calculations in the analytical instrument workstation {OTHER}, or a controlled {SPREADSHEET}, for repeated concentration arithmetic. Retain specimen work, substance identification, control interpretation and final analytical acceptance with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Some laboratories still repeat concentration and dilution arithmetic outside instrument software.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured formulas can apply explicit checked calibration and dilution records.
tasks.still_hard: Interference, matrix effects and degraded specimens can invalidate apparently precise concentrations.
tasks.human_edge: The technician judges method suitability and recognises when quantification is not supportable.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated arithmetic where it exists; identification and result acceptance remain human.

reach.learn: Communicate analytical uncertainty without inferring unsupported exposure or effect.

evidence.claim: Configured concentration calculations from checked analytical inputs are model knowledge; no digest case establishes forensic toxicology labour savings.

assumptions: Boundary is substance identification and analytical quantification, excluding general evidence interpretation, toxicological significance and formal external release.

Technician produces specimen ID, method version, units, calibration coefficients, calibration range, measured responses, sample mass/volume, dilution factors, control observations and reviewed exclusions during s1. All capture and suitability checks are counted; failed controls or missing fields return to manual investigation before s2.
OTHER is analytical instrument workstation. Prefer native validated calculations; existing automatic processing is excluded from the saving baseline.
research_questions: Can independent reference specimens expose unit, dilution and calibration-range errors before analytical acceptance?

already_counted.description: Physical analysis, checked inputs and final analytical review remain fully counted.

incremental.description: Maintain independently checked calculation versions and reference cases.
Laboratory systems administrator maintains controlled configuration access.

approvals.approved_version: Exact specimen, raw observations, calculation version and accepted result; changes void acceptance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=80 gross=20 net=12 after 8 upkeep. Zero when instruments already calculate concentrations; 3 if a small manual dilution calculation subset benefits.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: A limited arithmetic opportunity can reduce repetition while forensic merit review and evidence attribution remain independent human work.
reach: Coordinate analytical limitations with toxicologists and attribution uncertainty with specialist examiners.
role.ambitious_version: A technician who automates explicit arithmetic while preserving independent scrutiny of what the evidence means.
